rounds.fact: Pinterest launched by invite-only in 2010, and its signature masonry grid of pins was one of the first mainstream uses of that layout style on the web.
Juno offered free dial-up internet paid for entirely by advertising, and later merged with rival NetZero to survive the end of the free-ISP era.
Addicting Games grew rapidly during the mid-2000s Flash gaming boom, hosting thousands of free browser games at a time when installing a game usually still meant buying a physical disc.
HotBot launched in 1996 with a distinctly loud, colorful interface, and was one of the first search engines to index the full text of pages rather than just titles and keywords.
Gawker built its identity on gossipy, irreverent media and tech coverage, and its comment sections were an early influential experiment in giving readers real visibility on a media site.
